findings.title: Complex conditional type `TakeTwo` introduced
findings.body: The new `TakeTwo` conditional type is 18 lines long and deeply nested, making it hard to read and maintain. It is used only once in the file and could be simplified or extracted to a utility module to improve clarity.
findings.suggestion: type TakeTwo<T> = T extends [infer A0, infer A1] ? [A0, A1] : T extends [infer A0, infer A1, ...unknown[]] ? [A0, A1] : [undefined, undefined];

findings.title: Overly complex `StoreSetStateWithAction` type
findings.body: The new `StoreSetStateWithAction` type is 9 lines long and uses multiple conditional types, making it difficult to understand. It is defined to support a single use case and could be simplified or split into smaller, more focused types.
findings.suggestion: type StoreSetStateWithAction<S> = S extends { setState: (...a: infer A) => infer Sr } ? { setState: (...a: A) => Sr } : never;

findings.title: Complex generic type `Devtools` introduced
findings.body: The new `Devtools` generic type is 5 lines long and uses multiple generic parameters with complex constraints. It is used only once and could be simplified or split to improve readability.
findings.suggestion: type Devtools<T extends State> = (initializer: StateCreator<T, [], []>, options?: DevtoolsOptions) => StateCreator<T, [['zustand/devtools', never]], []>;

findings.title: Complex generic type `DevtoolsImpl` introduced
findings.body: The new `DevtoolsImpl` generic type is 4 lines long and uses a helper type `PopArgument` to manipulate function parameters. This adds unnecessary complexity for a single use case and could be simplified.
findings.suggestion: type DevtoolsImpl<T extends State> = (storeInitializer: StateCreator<T, [], []>, options: DevtoolsOptions) => StateCreator<T, [], []>;

findings.title: Type alias `NamedSet` redefined with different semantics
findings.body: The new `NamedSet` type alias redefines the existing type with a different structure (`WithDevtools<StoreApi<T>>['setState']`). This breaks the local convention where `NamedSet` was previously a function type with specific parameters. The new definition should align with the existing usage in the file.

findings.title: Function `devtoolsImpl` introduced with complex signature
findings.body: The new `devtoolsImpl` function has a complex signature with multiple generic parameters and a helper type `PopArgument`. This makes it harder to understand and maintain. The function could be simplified or split into smaller functions.
findings.suggestion: const devtoolsImpl: <T extends State>(fn: StateCreator<T, [], []>, options: DevtoolsOptions) => StateCreator<T, [], []> = (fn, options) => (set, get, api) => { ... };

findings.title: Type `Devtools` re-exported with inconsistent naming
findings.body: The `devtools` function is re-exported as `devtoolsImpl as unknown as Devtools`, which introduces an inconsistent naming convention. The export should follow the existing pattern in the file or be clearly documented.

summary.problem: The refactor introduces several complex types and functions that reduce readability and violate local naming conventions, making the code harder to maintain.
summary.done_well: The changes modernize the devtools middleware to use the latest Zustand patterns and TypeScript features, improving type safety and reducing boilerplate in downstream usage.
